questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question validates the ability to implement observability in a Docker DCA (Docker Certified Associate) multi-data center environment. It tests practical knowledge of wiring OpenTelemetry instrumentation into an API, configuring Jaeger as a distributed tracing backend, and coordinating per-tenant sampling through Docker Configs—all while operating behind a TLS-terminating edge proxy.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry SDK integration within a service API
- Jaeger as a distributed tracing backend with cross-DC replication
- Docker Config for centralized, runtime-based parameter management
- Per-tenant sampling strategies for cost-effective observability
- X-Tenant header propagation for multi-tenant trace correlation

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton

```yaml
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --providers.docker
      - --providers.docker.swarmMode
      - --entrypoints.websecure Address::443
      - --entrypoints.websecure.tls
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_JAEGER_ENDPOINT=jaeger:14250
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-service
    configs:
      - source: tenant-sampling
        target: /etc/sampling.json

  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.50
    environment:
      - COLLECTOR_REPLICATION_FACTOR=2
    ports:
      - "16686:16686"

configs:
  tenant-sampling:
    external: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests capability for complex, real-world docker-dca setups: SPIFFE SVIDs from Vault, Envoy as a policy-enforcing proxy, Consul KV-driven OPA policies, and geo-distributed canary rollouts with strict SLA boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-DC docker-dca deployment
- Vault SPIFFE SVID provisioning
- Envoy sidecar with mTLS and OPA RBAC via Consul KV
- Webhook-driven policy refresh
- Canary rollout discipline with latency/error budgets and automatic rollback

## Code Example
```javascript
# docker-compose.yml skeleton (YAML content displayed in a JS code block for formatting)
version: '3.8'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:stable
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    networks:
      - web
  api:
    image: myapi:latest
    networks:
      - web
    depends_on:
      - edge
  envoy:
    image: envoyproxy/envoy-alpine:v1.25.0
    networks:
      - web
# TLS, SPIFFE, and policy integration are configured via mounts/ENVs in real setup
networks:
  web:
    driver: overlay
```

# docker-compose.yml (skeleton)
version: '3.8'
services:

    ports:
      - 443:443

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to coordinate TLS edge routing with tenant-aware canary rollouts across two data centers using Docker DCA, Traefik rules, and Docker Configs. Encourages practical wiring, config rotation, and simple rollback semantics.

## Key Concepts
- Docker DCA multi-datacenter deployment
- Traefik Host-based routing and canary patterns
- Docker Config for per-tenant flag storage
- Canary rollout semantics and hot-reload

## Bootstrap Commands
```bash
# Create the tenant-canary Docker Config
echo 'tenant1,tenant2,tenant3' | docker config create tenant-canary -

# Deploy api-v1 (default backend)
docker stack deploy -c docker-compose.yml myapp
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml
```yaml
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --providers.docker
      - --providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
      - --entrypoints.websecure.address=:443
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

  api-v1:
    image: api:v1
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    labels:
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v1.rule=Host(`example.com`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v1.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v1.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.services.api-v1.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"

  api-v2:
    image: api:v2
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    labels:
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v2.rule=Host(`tenant1.example.com`,`tenant2.example.com`,`tenant3.example.com`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v2.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api-v2.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.services.api-v2.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"

configs:
  tenant-canary:
    external: true
```

## How It Works
- Traefik automatically discovers services via Docker labels
- Default traffic flows to api-v1 via the catch-all Host rule
- Tenant subdomains are explicitly routed to api-v2
- Adding tenants to the Docker Config and updating labels enables canary routing
- Rollback involves reverting labels or updating the subdomain list

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS implementation, Docker secrets management, and edge proxy configuration in a Swarm environment. Evaluates operational skills for secure service-to-service communication.

## Key Concepts
- Docker secrets for TLS certificate management
- Nginx mutual TLS verification and client certificate validation
- Client identity propagation to backend services via HTTP headers

## Code Example
```yaml
# skeleton docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - source: nginx_server_cert
        target: server.crt
      - source: nginx_server_key
        target: server.key
      - source: nginx_ca_cert
        target: ca.pem
    configs:
      - source: nginx_config
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
secrets:
  nginx_server_cert:
    external: true
  nginx_server_key:
    external: true
  nginx_ca_cert:
    external: true
configs:
  nginx_config:
    external: true
```

## Certificate Generation
```bash
# Create private CA
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca.key -out ca.pem

# Generate server certificate
openssl genrsa -out server.key 2048
openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out server.crt -days 365

# Generate client certificate
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.crt -days 365

# Create Docker secrets
docker secret create nginx_server_cert server.crt
docker secret create nginx_server_key server.key
docker secret create nginx_ca_cert ca.pem
```

## Testing Commands
```bash
# Test with client certificate
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Test without client certificate (should fail)
curl --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Verify client identity header
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api -v | grep X-Client-Subject
```
